"'''El Amor Que Perdimos'''" ([[English language|English]]: "The Love That We Lost") is a 2010 song by American singer [[Prince Royce]]. The song was released in January 2011 as the third single taken from Royce's [[Prince Royce (album)|eponymous debut studio album]] (2010). It won the [[Lo Nuestro Award for Tropical Song of the Year]].<ref name="Winners-2012">{{cite news|url=http://musica.univision.com/premio-lo-nuestro/backstage-pass/article/2012-02-16/ganadores-premio-lo-nuestro-2012|title=Ganadores de Premio Lo Nuestro 2012|work=[[Univision]]|publisher=[[Univision Communications]]|date=February 16, 2012|accessdate=September 27, 2013}}</ref>

'''''Prince Royce''''' is the debut studio album by American singer-songwriter [[Prince Royce]]; it was released on March 2, 2010, through [[Top Stop Music]]. The production was handled primarily by Andrés Hidalgo, with other contributions made by [[Sergio George]] (who also served as the album's executive producer), Eduardo Aguilar, George Meña, Bastiany, Gregory "Greko" Rojo and Nápoles. All songs were co-produced by Prince Royce and D'Lesly Lora.

In the United States, the album was a commercial success. Upon its US release, it debuted at number 16 on the [[Billboard Top Latin Albums|''Billboard'' Top Latin Albums]] chart. It eventually reached number one on both the US [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']] [[Tropical Albums]] and Top Latin Albums charts and was the best-selling Latin album of 2011 in the United States. It also peaked at number 77 on the all-genre [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] albums chart. In October 2011, ''Prince Royce'' was certified 3× Platinum ([[Latin music|Latin]] field) in the United States by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) and in 2020 it was certified 10× Platinum.<ref name="RIAA"/>

The album was also a commercial success in Chile, where it was certified 2× Platinum by the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] of Chile (IFPI Chile). The album was supported by four [[Single (music)|singles]]: "[[Stand by Me (Ben E. King song)#Prince Royce version|Stand By Me]]", "[[Corazón Sin Cara]]", "[[El Amor Que Perdimos]]" and "[[Mi Última Carta]]". The second single, "Corazón Sin Cara", reached number one on the [[Hot Latin Songs|''Billboard'' Hot Latin Songs]] chart in the US, where it was the best-performing Latin song of 2011.
